info.title: SuperTokens Core API (Mock)
info.description: Mock of the SuperTokens core: the service a backend SDK talks to over HTTP with an api-key header. Domain outcomes ride in the response body as a status string with HTTP 200 (for example WRONG_CREDENTIALS_ERROR); non-2xx is reserved for transport problems - a missing api key (401), an unsupported cdi-version (400), an unknown tenant (404). Every recipe path is tenant-scoped: both /recipe/... and the explicit /appid-{appId}/{tenantId}/recipe/... form are served.

get.description:
Return captured request/response logs.

WARNING: the unpaginated default response embeds a full copy of every
response body seen this session and grows without bound — late in a
session it can exceed what client tooling returns intact (long output
is often silently capped). Prefer `/audit/summary` for an overview, or
page through with `limit`/`offset` and `include_body=false` (drops the
bulky `response_body` field; `request_body` is always kept).

Defaults (no params = full dump, bodies included) are kept for
compatibility with the grading harness, which reads this endpoint
parameter-less and asserts on response_body content.
Clear the request log. Returns count of cleared entries.
Return aggregated summary of API usage.

One path, three recipes.

A backend SDK reaches this through its own recipe's router, so the core
knows which recipe is asking. Here the recipes share a path, so `recipeId`
picks explicitly; without it the query parameters decide, and an email alone
means emailpassword.
